title: Tarte Flambée
subtitle: Alsatian thin-crust tart with crème fraîche, onion, and lardons
excerpt: Tarte flambée (Flammkuchen in German) is an Alsatian thin-crust tart baked on a very hot stone or flat tray. The base is a simple bread dough rolled paper-thin and topped with crème fraîche, finely sliced onions, and smoked lardons. It bakes in 10 to 12 minutes at a very high temperature and should be eaten immediately.
sourceNotes: Tarte flambée originated as a way for Alsatian bakers to test whether their wood-fired ovens were hot enough. The name means 'flamed tart': the very high heat was originally provided by the dying embers of a wood fire. The dish is now associated with the harvest season in Alsace and Baden.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can be made up to 4 hours ahead and kept covered at room temperature.
recipe.temperatureNote: conventional oven, as hot as it will go

content.text: Tarte flambée is Alsatian pizza: a thin bread-dough base, a thin smear of crème fraîche, onion, and lardons. The key difference from pizza is that the base is rolled paper-thin (2 to 3 mm) and baked at the highest temperature your oven can reach. A pizza stone or a preheated heavy baking tray helps. It should have some char at the edges and take no more than 12 minutes.
Mix the flour, yeast, a pinch of salt, olive oil, and 150 ml warm water together into a rough dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes (no need for a full rise).

Heat the oven to its maximum temperature (ideally 250°C or higher) with a heavy baking tray inside. Divide the dough in half. Roll each piece on a lightly floured surface as thin as possible: 2 to 3 mm.
Season the crème fraîche with salt and white pepper. Spread a thin layer over each dough base, right to the edges. Scatter over the sliced onions and lardons.
Slide onto the hot baking tray (use a board or peel) and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are beginning to char and the lardons are cooked through. Eat immediately.

items.symptom: Base is soft and not crisp
items.cause: Oven was not hot enough or the tray was cold when the tarte went in
items.fix: Preheat the oven fully for at least 30 minutes and always preheat the baking tray. A cold tray produces a steamed base rather than a crisp one.

items.symptom: Topping is too wet and the crème fraîche has become watery
items.cause: Too thick a layer of crème fraîche, or the onions were not thin enough to cook quickly
items.fix: Spread the crème fraîche in an extremely thin layer: it should almost see-through. Slice onions paper-thin.

content.text: Tarte flambée is the social food of Alsace. It is served by the half-tart in restaurants called winstubs: traditional Alsatian wine bars. Diners eat several half-tartes between them, ordering different toppings as the evening progresses. The sweet version with fromage blanc and sugar is the customary end to the meal.
